definitions.explanation: A structure built along a waterfront where ships can load and unload cargo or passengers. Often evokes an atmospheric, slightly nostalgic image of port towns.

examples.japanese: {波止場|はとば}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{船|ふね}→船：00775_fune⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{停|と}まって⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: A ship is moored at the wharf.

examples.japanese: {波止場|はとば}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{魚釣|さかなつ}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧がいた。
examples.english: There were people fishing at the pier.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夕暮|ゆうぐ}れ→夕暮れ：07682_yuugure⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{波止場|はとば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{散歩|さんぽ}する→散歩する：26840_sanposuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。
examples.english: I like strolling along the wharf at dusk.

notes:
USAGE:
A somewhat literary or evocative word. In everyday speech, ⟦{港|みなと}→港：01512_minato⟧ (port, harbor) is more common. {波止場|はとば} often appears in literature, songs, and nostalgic descriptions of port towns.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {波止場|はとば}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧ (to wait at the wharf)
- {波止場|はとば}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風景|ふうけい}→風景：03591_fuukei⟧ (wharf scenery)
- {波止場|はとば}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧ (to work at the docks)

FORMS:
{波止|はと} (breakwater) + ⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧ (place). {波止|はと} comes from ⟦{波|なみ}→波：00868_nami⟧ (wave) + ⟦{止|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧ (to stop).
